profiles.title: Getting Started with Profiles
profiles.intro: Before you can apply for a service, you need the right profile. This guide explains how profiles work in the National Media Authority portal.

whatIsProfile.title: What is a profile?
whatIsProfile.content: A profile represents who you are applying as. Your account can hold profiles in two main categories:

individual.title: Individual
individual.description: For applying as a person, using your personal profile.

establishment.title: Establishment
establishment.description: For applying on behalf of a company or organization.

establishmentSubtypes.title: Establishment sub-types
establishmentSubtypes.content: An Establishment profile has a sub-type that reflects your organization, such as Commercial Entity, Government Entity, Advertising/Talent Management Agency, Free Zone, Shipping Company, Embassy, Consulate, or Cultural Club. The available sub-types depend on your organization and are set when the profile is created.

choosingProfile.title: Choosing the right profile for a service
choosingProfile.content: Each service defines which profiles may apply for it. A service may be open to Individual profiles, to specific Establishment sub-types, or to more than one profile type. You must apply using a profile that matches the service's requirements.

multipleProfiles.title: One account, multiple profiles
multipleProfiles.content: A single account can hold one Individual profile and one or more Establishment profiles. When you apply for a service, the application is tied to the profile you select — either your personal profile or one of your registered establishments.

addOrSwitch.title: Add or switch profiles as needed
addOrSwitch.addProfile: If your account has no profile that meets a service's requirements, add a new profile with the required category or establishment sub-type.
addOrSwitch.switchProfile: If you already have a qualifying profile but it is not the one currently in use, switch to it before applying.

verification.title: Verification and approval
verification.content: A newly created profile must be verified and approved before it can be used. While a profile is still under review, it cannot be used to apply for services. Once approved, the profile is ready and you can start submitting service requests.

profiles.guidance: This page is for guidance only. Actual profile creation, switching, and approval follow the portal's profile management and service eligibility rules.

serviceRequest.title: How to Submit a Service Request
serviceRequest.intro: Follow these steps to apply for a service in the portal.

signIn.title: Sign in and check your profile
signIn.content: Log in to your account and make sure you have a verified and approved profile that matches the service you want to apply for. If you don't have one yet, add the required profile first.

selectService.title: Select the service
selectService.content: Browse the service list and choose the service you want to apply for.

confirmProfile.title: Confirm the right profile
confirmProfile.content: The system checks whether your current profile type is eligible for the selected service. If it isn't, you'll be prompted to add a new profile or switch to a qualifying one before continuing.

completeApplication.title: Complete the application form
completeApplication.content: Fill in the required details and upload any supporting documents the service requires.

payment.title: Payment
payment.content: Some services are free and some are paid. For paid services, the timing of payment depends on the service:

payFirst.title: Pay first, then review
payFirst.description: For some services you complete the payment when you submit, and the review begins afterwards.

reviewFirst.title: Review first, then pay
reviewFirst.description: For other services the application is reviewed first, and payment is only required after it is approved

payment.timing: The portal will guide you on which applies and when payment is due for your selected service.

submitAndTrack.title: Submit and track
submitAndTrack.content: Once submitted, your application enters the review process. You can follow its status at any time under My Requests.

serviceRequest.guidance: This page is for guidance only. The actual application flow, eligibility checks, and payment timing follow each service's own rules.

refundRequest.title: How to Submit a Refund Request
refundRequest.intro: If you are eligible for a refund, you can request it in one of two ways.

paymentsOption.title: Option A — From the Payments page
paymentsOption.signIn: Sign in and go to the Payments page.
paymentsOption.findPayment: Find the payment record that is eligible for a refund.
paymentsOption.submit: Fill in the required details, such as the reason for the refund, and submit.

refundMenuOption.title: Option B — From the Refund menu
refundMenuOption.signIn: Sign in and open the Refund menu.
refundMenuOption.submit: Enter the required details, such as the payment/reference number and the reason for the refund, then submit.

track.title: Track your request
track.content: After submitting, your refund request is received and reviewed. You can follow its status at any time on the Refund page. Once approved, the refund is processed according to the original payment method and the applicable refund rules.

refundRequest.guidance: This page is for guidance only. Actual refund eligibility, channels, and timelines follow the applicable refund rules.
